entries.reason: the number a shader uses to name the buffer; the port's shaders are CPU kernels that take the buffer's bytes as a pointer, so the address is that pointer widened to 64 bits
entries.effect: a nonzero address, the same on every read while the buffer lives, and different for two live buffers; the value is the CPU address of the bytes, which is not Metal's GPU address, so the value is not compared
entries.source: SDK 16.4, Metal; the introduction 16.0 from the corpus surface of the 26.2 SDK; the relations measured on the host in tests/backports/device/buffer-probe/host-expectations.txt
